messages:
matt: quick sync — we're revisiting how we route requests when service tokens are opaque. tradeoffs: privacy vs routability. thoughts?
priya: opaque tokens are great for least-privilege + reduces leak surface, but edge routers can't make routing decisions without introspection.
sara: +1. introspection adds latency and load. can we put minimal routing hint outside the token? header or SNI? :thinking_face:
lee: headers are easiest but risk leaking tenant/project mapping to intermediate proxies. also breaks our desire to have interchangeable proxies.
matt: remembered earlier RFC about embedding a short routing key in the token header (not payload) — still feels leaky. we discussed hashed route keys that only our routers can reverse, any others?
priya: hashing helps but doesn't prevent correlation attacks if the same hash travels across services. ephemeral route keys (rotated per connection) are better but harder.
sara: what about an opaque token + a separate short-lived signed envelope that contains routing hints — routers validate envelope signature but cannot read other claims? basically envelope only for routing.
lee: that could work. example flow: client presents token T and envelope E. router verifies E.sig with RouterKey and reads E.route. Router uses route + forwards T to auth service if needed. prevents global leakage because envelope TTL is tiny.
matt: love the pattern. tradeoffs: extra roundtrip for envelope minting, and we need key management for RouterKey across regions. also complexity for fallback when envelope missing.
priya: operationally we can mint envelope at edge-issuers (edge-auth) while exchanging long token. clients do one-time exchange. sequence: 1) client sends creds -> edge-issuer returns (T,E). 2) client uses (T,E) for requests.
sara: fallback: if E missing, router can do introspect(T) to get route. keep introspect as fallback only.
lee: implement notes: E format: base64url {route: "proj:123", exp: 171..., nonce: "..."} signed with ed25519. small size < 128 bytes.
matt: security Q — what if attacker captures (T,E) on public network? E short TTL mitigates. also recommend encryping route inside E so intermediate routers that shouldn't see route can't. but router must decrypt -> need KMS accessible to routers.
priya: encrypting route inside envelope means router needs decryption key; same leak surface. but it prevents casual logging of route at other components that see E. good trade.
lee: propose POC: implement envelope minting in edge-auth, routers validate signature, decrypt route with RouterKMS, fallback introspect path, and TTL 30s. Start with internal-only rollout.
sara: +1. small concerns: metrics and tracing — we need to ensure envelope nonce ties to trace id for debugging.
matt: agreed. action items: @priya will draft short RFC with envelope format and key rotation plan, @lee will sketch router validation flow, @sara will list observability needs. I'll follow up to schedule 30-min sync next week.
auth-bot: note created: RFC draft requested by matt — due in 5d.
